cells.name: Continuity and responsiveness
cells.example: T4 answers T3's acceptance with 'But relationships require shared effort to flourish.'
cells.limitation: T7 ignores T6's boundaries-versus-manipulation point and repeats T4's nudge idea.

cells.name: Development of ideas
cells.example: T6 distinguishes speaking to clarify your boundaries from speaking to manipulate; section D reuses it.
cells.limitation: T7 and T8 restate T4 and T5 without adding a new distinction.

cells.name: Exploration of central tensions
cells.example: T3 versus T4 sets acceptance of the friend's nature against shared effort.
cells.limitation: Nobody raises friend's possible reasons (capacity, style) or whether planning itself bothers the user.

cells.name: Integration of perspectives
cells.example: T6 conditionally accepts speaking: 'If you speak, do so to clarify your own boundaries.'
cells.limitation: T5 'Exactly' and T8 'Precisely' merge Architect and Negotiator without either qualifying the other.

cells.name: Progress toward understanding
cells.example: Section E sharpens to whether the friend is oblivious or indifferent.
cells.limitation: T9 ends on accept-or-walk-away, an endpoint already implicit in T3.

cells.name: Faithful engagement
cells.example: T4 restates T3's acceptance before answering it with mutual effort.
cells.limitation: T2 dismisses T1 as 'a passive stance'; T6 attacks a 'demand' nobody made.

cells.name: Substance of challenges
cells.example: T4 tests T3: if stopping produces nothing, the bond may be thin.
cells.limitation: No objection names an assumption and what breaks; T3's view is never answered directly.

cells.name: Accuracy and support
cells.example: T1 habit framing plausibly fits Brooks's emphasis on unconscious social patterns.
cells.limitation: T3 quote reads as a modern paraphrase, not Meditations; T5 garbles 'separate the people from the problem'.

cells.name: Calibration and transparency
cells.example: T1 hedges: 'You might simply be the designated initiator.'
cells.limitation: T2 asserts 'You have an unmet need'; T9 treats silence as a definite answer.

cells.name: Intellectual honesty and revision
cells.example: T6 partly yields: speaking is allowed if aimed at boundaries.
cells.limitation: No mind concedes a point or revises a claim across T1 to T9.

cells.name: Identification of the actual concern
cells.example: Section A names the one-sided initiating and the question of addressing it.
cells.limitation: Whether the hurt is the planning burden or feeling unwanted is never distinguished.

cells.name: Meaningful use of personal context
cells.example: T8 uses 'you value the time' from the user's 'it's lovely'.
cells.limitation: T4 proposes a test the user already ran: 'if I stop texting, nothing happens'.

cells.name: Fit with goals and values
cells.example: T8 keeps the user's enjoyment of meetings alongside the planning burden.
cells.limitation: T6 and T9 impose Stoic acceptance and walking away as the speakers' own values.

cells.name: Attention to constraints and stakes
cells.example: Section E names the risk of losing the connection.
cells.limitation: Section E overstates a gentle talk as risking the friendship; no other stakes weighed.

cells.name: Responsiveness to information
cells.example: Section E branches on oblivious versus indifferent friend.
cells.limitation: No question about friend's circumstances, how long this has lasted, or other signs of care.

cells.name: Clarification of desires and motivations
cells.example: Section D frames speaking up as honoring your own needs.
cells.limitation: T2 declares an unmet need for reciprocity; no alternative motives offered.

cells.name: Examination of assumptions
cells.example: T1 questions the assumption that silence means indifference, offering habit instead.
cells.limitation: T9 reasserts silence as the answer; the assumption is never opened to the user.

cells.name: Clarification of values and priorities
cells.example: Section D sets equitable dynamic against accepting others' limits.
cells.limitation: The user is never asked which matters more to them.

cells.name: Recognition of fears and outside expectations
cells.example: T9 mentions walking away 'without resentment', hinting at resentment.
cells.limitation: Fear of rejection or of seeming needy is never named or examined.

cells.name: Agency and reflective ownership
cells.example: Section E offers conditionals the user can place themselves within.
cells.limitation: T2, T6, T9 issue directives ('you should', 'you must') rather than distinctions to weigh.

cells.name: Definition of the decision and options
cells.example: Options: speak up (T5), gentle nudge (T7), accept or walk away (T9).
cells.limitation: No limited step such as asking the friend to plan the next meeting.

cells.name: Explanation of tradeoffs
cells.example: Section E contrasts the risk of speaking with peace of acceptance.
cells.limitation: Costs of speaking up never spelled out; acceptance's ongoing cost to the user unstated.

cells.name: Identification of decisive conditions
cells.example: Section E: the conversation diagnoses oblivious versus genuinely indifferent.
cells.limitation: No observable sign named that would show which, or which option each favours.

cells.name: Treatment of uncertainty
cells.example: Section E names the friend's intent as the key unknown.
cells.limitation: Friend's circumstances and the user's tolerance for planning are not separated as unknowns.

cells.name: Proportionate next steps
cells.example: T8 phrasing: value the time but feel the burden of planning.
cells.limitation: No step for what follows the friend's reply beyond T9's accept-or-leave.

cells.name: Accessible language
cells.example: T8 is plain and concrete about what to say.
cells.limitation: T1 'designated initiator in your social ecosystem' adds abstraction.

cells.name: Traceable arguments and references
cells.example: T4 'But' clearly answers T3.
cells.limitation: T2 'That is a passive stance' is ambiguous: T1's view or the friend.

cells.name: Manageable pacing and turn length
cells.example: All nine turns fall within 25 to 65 words.
cells.limitation: Strict A-B-C rotation gives every turn the same length and weight.

cells.name: Distinguishable positions and voices
cells.example: The Stoic in T3 and T9 uses rhetorical questions and acceptance.
cells.limitation: Architect and Negotiator become one position from T5; no explicit position change.

cells.name: Economy and sustained attention
cells.example: Turns are short and section E is compact.
cells.limitation: T8 repeats T5; T6 and T9 both say accept the friendship as it is.

cells.name: Meaningful stakes and tension
cells.example: T4: 'the bond might be thinner than you think.'
cells.limitation: Two minds agree early, leaving the Stoic as the only tension.

cells.name: Surprise and reversals
cells.example: T6 Stoic shifts slightly to permit speaking for boundaries.
cells.limitation: No reversal or surprise anywhere in T1 to T9.

cells.name: Personality and expressive voice
cells.example: T3 Stoic opens: 'Why be troubled by a friend's nature?'
cells.limitation: Architect and Negotiator speak in a shared advice-column register.

cells.name: Memorable delivery
cells.example: T1 image of the user as 'designated initiator'.
cells.limitation: No analogy, vivid example or sharp line beyond T1 and T9.

cells.name: Anticipation and emotional movement
cells.example: T9 'And if they remain silent? Then you have your answer.'
cells.limitation: Even rhythm throughout; T5 to T8 agreement flattens movement.

strengths: T6 Stoic introduces speaking to clarify boundaries rather than to change the friend, reused in section D.
Section E frames a low-stakes conversation as diagnosing oblivious versus indifferent.
T8 Negotiator offers usable phrasing: value the time, name the planning burden.
weaknesses: No mind asks the user anything; friend's circumstances and other signs of care never branched (T1 to T9, section E).
Architect and Negotiator collapse into agreement from T5 ('Exactly', 'Precisely'); no concessions or revisions anywhere.
T3 Stoic presents a likely modern paraphrase as Meditations text; T4 proposes a test the user already ran.

symptoms.observed: No question about friend's circumstances or other signs of care; missing facts never branched.
symptoms.evidence: You need to test if they value the connection itself.

symptoms.observed: Negotiator agrees with Architect outright twice, without qualifying or reshaping either view.
symptoms.evidence: Exactly. By communicating your feelings without blame

symptoms.observed: Proposes stopping initiation as a test, though the user already observed that outcome.
symptoms.evidence: If you stop initiating and nothing happens

symptoms.observed: Declares the user's motive as fact; no alternative motives offered for the user to weigh.
symptoms.evidence: You have an unmet need for reciprocity.

symptoms.observed: Presents a likely paraphrase as Meditations text; misstates a Getting to Yes principle.
symptoms.evidence: As it is written, You have power over your mind

findings.description: Line introduced 'As it is written' resembles a popular modern paraphrase, not a recognised Meditations translation; no translation named.
'Focus on the relationship, not the person' inverts Getting to Yes's 'separate the people from the problem'.
Meditations dated 161; usually dated c. 170 to 180, 161 being Marcus's accession.
Silence after one conversation is treated as a definite answer about the friend's regard.

rubric_fit_notes: The T3 quotation concern rests on memory only, so no cap entry; C2.3 rated on suspected findings.
question_type_note: Decision question about raising a one-sided friendship; every cell read as written.
